final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest MSA mutant frequency (0.26, full coverage) in the N-terminal activation domain, indicating strong evolutionary tolerance with potential for functional modulation of transactivation.
Conservative K->R near the core domain with solid combined evidence (MSA freq 0.116, full coverage; positive PLM), preserving basic character and viability.
Strongest PLM plausibility in the pool (0.40) with decent MSA tolerance (0.10) in the variable C-terminal region, posing low risk to Tat function.

stop_reason.detail: Available informative tools (MSA, PLM) have been applied and no remaining tool can directly measure Tat transactivation, so further evidence would not alter the Top-3.

history.rationale: Conservative acidic substitution in the acidic N-terminal region (Pro-rich/acidic domain); may fine-tune charge interactions involved in co-factor recruitment without disrupting folding.
Conservative acidic substitution in the N-terminal acidic region, unlikely to disrupt TAR-binding or co-factor recruitment.
Modest MSA (0.06) and near-neutral PLM (0.007); conservative substitution in the acidic N-terminus, retained as a mid-tier candidate.
Position 17 lies just before the Cys-rich domain; modest side-chain change could influence activation domain conformation while remaining chemically plausible.
Mild polar substitution in a variable region between the acidic and C-rich domains.
Highest MSA mutant frequency (0.26, full coverage) in the N-terminal activation domain; H at 17 is evolutionarily common, implying tolerance with potential functional modulation.
Conservative Lys-to-Arg in the core region near the Cys-rich domain; retains positive charge that may support Cyclin T1/P-TEFb interactions.
Conservative Lys->Arg near the cysteine-rich core; may preserve metal-binding architecture while modulating acetylation-dependent activity.
R never observed at position 28 across 69 homologs and PLM is near zero — strong evolutionary constraint argues against despite chemical conservatism.
Another conservative charge-preserving change in the core domain; small conformational tweak may improve transactivation complex stability.
Adjacent conservative substitution to K28R; both retained pending MSA/PLM evidence on which is better tolerated.
Conservative K->R with the best combined evidence: MSA freq 0.116 (full coverage) and PLM 0.104; preserves basic-region character near the core domain.
Within the arginine-rich TAR-binding motif; Lys retains basicity but alters RNA-binding geometry, potentially strengthening TAR interaction or reducing unproductive binding.
Edge of the basic TAR-binding domain; conservative but core function risk.
In the critical basic/TAR-binding region with very low entropy (0.43) and near-zero PLM; high risk of disrupting RNA binding, so demoted.
Basic ARM residue; charge-conserving substitution could modulate TAR RNA affinity and nuclear localization properties.
Inside the basic domain; risky but conservative charge-preserving swap.
Zero MSA frequency in the highly conserved arginine-rich RNA-binding motif (entropy 0.39) and near-zero PLM; likely to impair TAR binding and transactivation.

rejection.reason: Zero MSA frequency in the highly conserved arginine-rich RNA-binding motif (entropy 0.39) and near-zero PLM; likely to impair TAR binding and transactivation.

history.rationale: Glutamine-rich region substitution adding a negative charge; may improve interactions with positive patches on transcriptional machinery.
Q60 is in the variable hinge after the basic domain; charge change may modulate interactions, evidence needed.
Low but positive evidence with reduced MSA coverage (0.59); conservative Q->E keeps it viable as backup.
Conservative basic substitution in the auxiliary C-terminal region; plausibly tolerated while subtly altering co-factor contacts.
K71 is a key P-TEFb recruitment residue acetylated for cyclin T1 release; K->R may alter acetylation dynamics favorably, but high risk.
Zero MSA frequency, very low entropy (0.38) and low coverage; the position is tightly constrained, demoting it.
Ser-to-Ala reduces phosphorylation-dependent regulation at a C-terminal Ser; might stabilize an active conformation but carries modest risk.
C-terminal variable tail, low functional constraint; low priority.
Strongest PLM plausibility in the pool (0.40) and decent MSA tolerance (0.10); C-terminal region is variable and tolerant, low risk to viability.
